upstreams.name: Hyprland
upstreams.packaging_policy: Provides hyprland under the distinct hyprland-obsidience package identity so repository updates cannot silently erase the reviewed patches. Rebuild against changed shared-library ABIs; do not bypass dependency checks.
upstreams.adaptation: Used as the live Wayland compositor for Samsung, USB-C, and logical DP-4. Obsidience supplies its own minimal Lua configuration, supported custom layout provider, and shell surfaces. Native CSS gaps retain compositor-owned pointer hit-testing and native inner glow renders the low-rate OLED border treatment. One downstream source patch makes tiled pointer hit-testing follow the visible front-to-back order required when custom-layout tile bounds overlap. A second forwards native tiled-resize deltas and the grabbed corner to an optional Lua layout callback while preserving the existing recalculate-only fallback. A third restores native click-to-focus when a layer surface owns the keyboard, or keyboard focus is empty, while the clicked window remains the remembered active window. It retains pointer constraints, held-button handling, popup focus and session-lock enforcement in the existing compositor input path. No Hyprland visual design is copied.

upstreams.name: Quickshell
upstreams.adaptation: Used as the Qt Quick and Wayland shell runtime. Its WlSessionLock and WlSessionLockSurface types own the secure ext-session-lock surfaces, while PamContext delegates authentication to the system PAM stack. One two-line compatibility patch supplies Qt WebEngine's documented host preconditions: a valid argv[0] for Chromium and shared graphics contexts selected before the first application object. v0.3.2 contains the upstream afb2c27 session-lock reentrancy fix that was previously backported. A two-line follow-up preserves the pre-unlock state so the existing locked property emits its false transition after release. The recipe asserts the upstream commit, the touched source files and both patches by hash, and records the produced binary hash in the runtime directory name and BUILDINFO; a Qt update is a plain rebuild. The distro quickshell package remains the IPC client (/usr/bin/qs); its IPC protocol is unchanged between 0.3.1 and 0.3.2. Obsidience owns the QML presentation and lock policy; no upstream visual design was copied.

upstreams.name: Qt WebEngine
upstreams.license: LGPL-3.0-only or GPL-3.0-only or commercial license, with bundled component licenses
upstreams.adaptation: Used as the installed QML WebEngineView runtime for the existing loopback-only Three.js graph renderer on the selected secure lock Surface. The web view is presentation-only and receives no credentials; password input remains native QML and authentication remains exclusively in Quickshell PamContext through the system PAM stack. No Qt WebEngine source was copied. The same installed runtime now hosts the ordinary desktop graph stages and native graph viewers. Local canvas capture/WebRTC streams transfer stage frames without a second viewer graph or simulation. Individual Knowledge views borrow the stage renderer and live clouds for an isolated camera pass. The presenter disables only GpuMemoryBufferReadbackFromTexture because this Qt Vulkan path cannot allocate its optional buffer; native capture remained functional with no failed-buffer errors. No upstream implementation was copied.

upstreams.name: Omarchy Quattro lock lifecycle
upstreams.adaptation: Obsidience adopts the narrow lock-lifecycle pattern: Hyprland permits its sole shell to reclaim an ext-session-lock after that client dies, compositor LOCK state is read from monitor blockers, active-lock development restarts are refused, and service startup reclaims only a stranded lock. Obsidience retains its own service, IPC, lock UI, PAM policy, and visual design.

upstreams.name: Omarchy quattro theme system
upstreams.adaptation: Obsidience independently applies two bounded reference patterns: one semantic palette projects into shell and supported application-native theme tokens, and one warm shell host loads small modular UI components. Omarchy source, visual design, shell scripts, Hyprland configuration, IPC, plugin runtime, and package authority were not imported.

upstreams.name: Voxtype dictation waveform reference
upstreams.adaptation: Visual reference only: a bounded recent amplitude history displayed oldest-left/newest-right with a quiet centerline. Obsidience independently renders its existing Realtime microphone-level telemetry as native QML bars beside streaming recognized text. No Voxtype source, audio capture, recognizer, IPC, typing path, daemon, or OSD host is imported. Levels are normalized volume samples, not a raw PCM min/max envelope.

upstreams.name: wlrctl private pointer transport
upstreams.adaptation: The existing Shell adapter privately invokes one bounded native client. The upstream button/frame sequence and real Wayland sync-callback pattern are adapted to exact output-name binding, output-local absolute motion, a positioned receipt followed by one controller commit, and a final acknowledged receipt. Disconnect, malformed or missing commit, output changes, and deadlines fail nonzero without replay. The helper owns no target identity, observation, permission, Task, Tool, daemon, or semantic success authority. The existing Shell Scene and Computer Use owner retain fresh identity, geometry, visibility, lock, grounding, cancellation, and postcondition checks. Callback acknowledgement means compositor protocol processing, never application acceptance. No wlrctl CLI, window matching, keyboard, relative pointer, or generic action surface is imported. The 2026-09-21 bounded drag extension uses the same native pointer and adds ten acknowledged motion steps between press and release. Every step requires a fresh controller commit after existing target, focus, lock and cancellation guards. EOF, cancellation, deadline and termination release a held button before destroying the pointer. The Shell admits only one pending input operation, without a queue.

upstreams.name: wlr virtual pointer protocol
upstreams.adaptation: The build reads the exact hash-checked installed v2 protocol XML and uses installed wayland-scanner and libwayland-client. Generated headers, protocol C, XML copyright notice, adapted source and the executable remain in a content-addressed runtime candidate outside the repository. build-pointer does not select a current runtime or connect to Wayland. The optional output argument is a compositor mapping suggestion, so the parent verifies the observed real cursor position before commit.

upstreams.name: Codex Harness lifecycle patterns
upstreams.adaptation: Independent Python implementation of lifecycle-owned provider connections, call identity and terminal outcomes, cursor-based public trace recovery, and exact-active-turn steering. The existing Obsidience executor, SQLite ledger, Conversation and Model runtime remain owners. Durable pre-dispatch receipts and replay admission are Obsidience-specific. No Codex Rust code, SDK, model, agent, process server or runtime dependency is imported.

upstreams.name: psutil
upstreams.adaptation: Installed Python dependency for the native Hardware pane read-only monitor API. Uses maintained CPU/core, memory/swap, disk/network cumulative counters, and bounded process identity/name/CPU/RSS sampling; existing host inventory owns GPU/hwmon data. Obsidience adds one lock-protected on-demand cache, safe deltas, availability projection, and native QML presentation using its existing ShellTheme and components. No upstream source or telemetry daemon imported. Public process_iter and oneshot collection reuse the upstream process cache with pre/post identity validation; process arguments are not projected or persisted. Physical interface selection excludes internal traffic from the summary.

upstreams.name: util-linux lsblk

upstreams.name: xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland
upstreams.packaging_policy: Provides xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland under the distinct xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland-obsidience package identity so a distribution rebuild cannot silently replace the backported capture fixes. Retire it once a distribution release contains all three fixes.
upstreams.adaptation: Backport three merged upstream capture fixes onto the installed 1.4.1 base: preserve capture callbacks across buffer starvation and format renegotiation, and advertise the actual DMA-BUF plane layout with DMA-specific buffer parameters. The ordinary portal remains the sole Discord screen-share backend; no replacement capture service or restart loop.
